note_truncation: p_x restricted to (0.05,0.95): the uncertain-middle regime; H5 reconstructs the full benchmark by adding reliable (p~1) mass.

citations.tau2_bench: arXiv:2506.07982 (Barres,Narasimhan et al. 2025, Sierra) -- dual-control reliability

H1_reliability_decay.claim: mean accuracy 0.674 collapses to pass^5=0.235: reporting only pass^1 overstates 5-trial reliability by 43.9 pp; naive mu^k UNDER-states true pass^k by 0.096 (Jensen, dispersion inflates).

H2_moment_expansion.claim: pass^k = mu^k + C(k,2)mu^{k-2}sigma^2 + C(k,3)mu^{k-3}m3 + ...; at k=3 the 3rd-order form is EXACT (err 1.1e-16, p^3 is degree-3) -- a closed validation. At k=6 the naive mu^k errs 0.0976; adding just the sigma^2 dispersion term removes 83% of that error, proving per-task variance is the first-order reliability correction, not a second-order nuisance.

H3_scissor.claim: at k=5 best-of-k reaches 0.967 while reliability pass^5=0.235 (scissor gap 0.732). Dispersion is DOUBLE-EDGED with OPPOSITE signs vs the homogeneous baseline: it RAISES reliability pass^k by +0.096 (p^k convex: always-pass tasks dominate the all-k set) but LOWERS best-of pass@k by -0.029 ((1-p)^k convex: always-fail tasks can never be rescued). A benchmark that reports only the rising pass@k curve hides a brittle agent the falling pass^k exposes.

H4_equal_mean_diff_var.claim: Two task sets with IDENTICAL mean accuracy (0.674) but variance 0.037 vs 0.114 give pass^5 = 0.235 vs 0.520: a benchmark that ranks only by mean accuracy CANNOT rank deployment reliability -- the higher-variance set is more reliable at large k (polarized into always/never), the tau2-Bench motivation for reporting pass^k.

H5_full_reconstruction.claim: Adding reliable (p~1) mass w1=0.60 to match the reported mean reward 0.869, the FULL-benchmark pass^5 = 0.694 while the naive mu^5 = 0.497: even at the benchmark's high accuracy, the Jensen reliability excess is 0.197 -- dispersion is a first-order term, so headline pass^1 must be paired with a pass^k reliability column (the same sigma^2_p that drives Pillar-2 ZVF collapse).
